chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever recites all the Musabbihaat before sleeping will not die until he sees Al-Qaim; and if he dies, he will be in the vicinity of Muhammad the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الْقَائِمَ: Al-Qaim, a title for the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, referring to his future appearance.
key_terms.الْمُسَبِّحَاتِ: The six chapters of the Quran (Surahs 17, 57, 59, 61, 62, 64, and 87) known for frequently mentioning the glorification of God.
key_terms.جِوَارِ: Vicinity, proximity, or neighborhood, often used in Islamic texts to denote spiritual closeness or being under the protection of a revered figure.

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting the Musabbihaat before sleeping according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, the 'Musabbihaat' refer to the six Quranic chapters beginning with the glorification formula 'Subhana', specifically Surah Al-Asr, Al-Kawthar, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas, and At-Takathur. This narration from Imam al-Sadiq links the spiritual discipline of nightly recitation to eschatological hope, promising the reciter the privilege of witnessing the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (Al-Qaim) or dwelling in the spiritual vicinity of the Prophet if they pass away before his advent.
